statement: Negative-transposition involutions in the full three-cusp loop-outer group correspond, by explicitly inverse marked extension constructions, to four-cusp V4 actions containing the specified standard free positive double-cover deck involution and a double-transposition involution of the same negative 2-adic multiplier. The latter involution has a torsion-free center-free extension. No separator used by D29's exchanged two-pants construction is invariant under a commuting single-transposition deck action; an additional deck action must move the separator.
where_proved: Part D, statement D.37; work/part_c/d37.tex; code/part_c/negative_transposition_d37.py
depends_on: A.7; D.28; D.29; the full profinite Brown restriction theorem
manuscript_passages: Part D(b) and D(d) of the task; §24, folio 147 verso, scan 293; §30, folios 194–196, scans 383–387; §31, folios 198–199 verso, scans 391–394.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Both covering and descent maps are specified on presentations and the geometric deck action is part of the marked data.
notes: The converse requires the explicitly specified standard deck action, not merely an arbitrary positive involution with torsion-free extension. The separator obstruction concerns preservation of the same two-pants graph only. Explicit noncommuting and commuting geometric deck representatives demonstrate why it does not exclude a deck action moving that separator. No existence of the extra deck symmetry for D29's mixed-sign action is asserted.
